task: Add project and actor-snapshot attribution to activity_events (36 emit sites, 10 files) plus a new project-scoped, project-admin-or-platform-admin-authorized read endpoint, leaving the existing global endpoint untouched.

key_reasoning.reason: Base XL on criteria alone (data model, migration, repository, service, router, security layer — 6 components, multiple subsystems, new abstractions for actor-snapshot and the admin-or-project-admin authz combinator); bumped to XXL because activity_events is a core shared utility spanning project/user/budget domains and the change affects all three workflows simultaneously.

Base L (no exact precedent for combining the denormalized-snapshot pattern with a new admin-or-project-admin authz guard, moderate security implications, rollback plan needed via migration). Bumped twice per the rubric's auto-bump rules: the closest authorization precedent (project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access) doesn't fully cover the new project-scoped combinator and has no located test coverage of its own; and the AC enumerate specific defensive cases (personal-project exclusion, actor-deleted snapshot, project-deleted snapshot, deterministic pagination on timestamp ties) with no existing test template for any of them. Further reinforced by the authorization red flag.

36 emit sites collapse to 10 modified files, plus activity_models.py, activity_repository.py, activity_event_service.py and authentication.py (~14 modified), plus new migration, new router, new API models, and new tests (~4-6 new) — matches the XL band (11-15 modified, 4-6 new, multiple subsystems).

Base L (data model/DB-persistence with a schema migration, service, API, and security/infrastructure layers — 3-4 layers including persistence). Bumped to XL via the 'changes database schema significantly' red flag (new indexed columns against a table with 29 existing Alembic heads to reconcile).
